transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-10-27
Start: 14:00 PDT
Duration: 48 minutes
Attendees: Alex Chen (Redwood AE), Priya Kapoor (Redwood SE), Marcus Lee (Aurelia - Procurement), Dina Ortiz (Aurelia - Counsel), Samira Khan (Aurelia - CISO)

Auto Summary (auto-generated):
Redwood and Aurelia Health kicked off a combined legal/technical onboarding to align on DPA/MSA redlines, SLA expectations, and Aurelia's data classification and residency constraints. Key concerns: patient PII classification, on-prem vs VPC options, KMS integration, and audit log retention. Actions: Redwood to circulate DPA redline; Aurelia to provide data classification matrix; plan technical deep-dive for private deployment.

Topics:
- DPA redlines and MSA routing
- SLA metrics and uptime/latency targets
- Data classification and residency limits (PHI/PII)
- KMS, SSO, and audit logs
- Pilot/benchmark plan and timelines

Transcript:
[00:00:00] Alex Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick roll call — Alex from Redwood, Priya is with me.
[00:00:07] Marcus Lee: Hey Alex, Marcus here. Dina, Samira on from legal and security.
[00:00:11] Dina Ortiz: Hi all. Sorry for joining a minute late.
[00:00:15] Priya Kapoor: No worries, Dina. We'll jump in. Agenda: line items on the DPA redlines you sent last week, plus a walkthrough of how data classification maps to our Private and Dedicated options.
[00:00:28] Marcus Lee: Yep that sounds right. For context, Aurelia runs a mix of PHI and non-sensitive customer data. Our procurement team needs to understand whether Redwood's hosted API can be used for low-risk data and what triggers private deployment.
[00:00:40] Samira Khan: And from security, we need clarity on KMS, SSO, audit log retention and the chain of custody for any patient identifiers. Also curious about egress controls and region restrictions.
[00:00:52] Alex Chen: Great, we'll address each. On the DPA/MSA: legal already noted a few redlines, Dina you flagged the data processing sub-clauses and the breach notification timelines?
[00:01:03] Dina Ortiz: Yeah, specifically the breach notif window was ambiguous — the template said 'prompt' and our policy is 72 hours. We need explicit 72-hour notice, and we want an SLA credit if notification is late.
[00:01:15] Alex Chen: Okay, that's reasonable. We'll propose a clear 72-hour clause in the redline. Priya, do you want to cover how that ties to our incident response and audit logs?
[00:01:24] Priya Kapoor: Sure — Redwood collects audit traces for all requests in Hosted mode for 90 days by default, with longer retention available as an add-on. For Dedicated and Private deployments, logs live in the customer's VPC or on-prem store, and retention is controlled by you and your KMS. There's a couple of places where our standard DPA language was generic and we can make it explicit: log retention, access controls, and the timeframe for forensic deliverables.
[00:01:47] Marcus Lee: When you say 'add-on', is that extra cost? Procurement will need pricing buckets.
[00:01:52] Alex Chen: Yes, longer retention and export services can be priced as an add-on. We'll include rough numbers in the follow-up.
[00:01:59] Samira Khan: We also need to ensure keys are customer-owned for PHI workflows. Does Redwood support bring-your-own-key (BYOK) with HSM/KMS integration?
[00:02:09] Priya Kapoor: We support KMS integrations for Private deployments and for Dedicated in most cases; in Hosted we use envelope encryption with Redwood-managed keys by default, but we offer a customer KMS option for enterprise customers with private instances. There's some nuance: true HSM-backed key material for multi-tenant hosted endpoints is limited, so if BYOK with HSM is mandatory, Private or Dedicated is the recommended path.
[00:02:33] Dina Ortiz: That aligns with concerns. For compliance evidence we'll need SOC 2 report and specific statements around key separation. Do you have SOC 2 and pen-test artifacts?
[00:02:42] Alex Chen: Yes, Redwood has a SOC 2 Type II report; we'll share a redacted copy through our secure portal. We also have recent pen test summary — I'll attach both.
[00:02:52] [00:02:52] Marcus Lee: Quick question about data residency: Aurelia requires 'at-rest' storage of PHI to be within the US only. Does Redwood support region pinning for hosted instances?
[00:03:03] Priya Kapoor: Yes, hosted tenants can be pinned to regions for data-at-rest and processing. For stronger guarantees we recommend Dedicated or Private where you control the VPC region. For hosted, we have data residency controls but the contract must reflect those guarantees.
[00:03:18] Alex Chen: On SLAs — typical hosted SLA is 99.9% with latency targets per model. For enterprise customers we can negotiate higher uptime commitments under Dedicated capacity. What are your success criteria?
[00:03:29] Marcus Lee: Procurement needs a 99.95% uptime commitment if we put PHI on your platform. Otherwise we're limited to non-PHI workloads. Is 99.95 achievable on Dedicated?
[00:03:39] Priya Kapoor: 99.95 is within the Dedicated offering with the appropriate capacity commitments and SLOs; we'll need to pin capacity and include a runbook. Also discuss failover — cross-region replication — that affects cost.
[00:03:51] Samira Khan: Cost vs latency trade-off. If we require cross-region replicas for HA, that will increase costs. We'll want a clear pricing estimate tied to the SLA level.
[00:04:02] Alex Chen: Understood. We'll include a cost delta for 99.9 vs 99.95 and for cross-region failover.
[00:04:08] Dina Ortiz: Back to the DPA — there's language about subcontractors and processors. Who are the main infra subprocessors for Redwood? We need a security subprocessor list.
[00:04:18] Priya Kapoor: We maintain a subprocessor list and can provide it; major cloud providers are listed, and for Dedicated we avoid multi-tenant infra where possible. We'll share the current roster in the follow-up.
[00:04:29] [00:04:29] Marcus Lee: Regarding onboarding timeline — procurement wants to know how long from signature to production pilot. Can you give a ballpark?
[00:04:36] Alex Chen: If it's Hosted with a non-PHI scope, you can be live in days. For Dedicated with provisioning and capacity tuning, typical provisioning is 2-4 weeks. Private on-prem can be 6-12 weeks depending on networking and security approvals.
[00:04:50] Samira Khan: Networking approvals are the bottleneck for us; NAT rules, egress approvals — if it's Private we have our own KMS and firewall rules to enforce.
[00:04:58] Priya Kapoor: For Private we ship an installer and a runbook; we usually coordinate with your infra team for ports and certs. We can provide a pre-flight checklist.
[00:05:07] Dina Ortiz: Also need to flag a legal ask — we want to shorten the indemnity cap for GDPR-adjacent items. Is Redwood open to discussing liability limits tied to the subscription value?
[00:05:18] Alex Chen: We can discuss; standard practice is to tie indemnity caps to a multiple of fees. I'll ask Commercial to propose a couple options.
[00:05:26] [00:05:26] Marcus Lee: On the technical side, can you describe what 'Private' actually looks like? Is it a full air-gapped install or a managed private control plane?
[00:05:34] Priya Kapoor: Private has two deployment flavors: managed private control plane (Redwood helps with upgrades but control plane endpoints are customer network-accessible) and fully on-prem package where the control plane is inside your data center. We do support an air-gapped install for customers with strict requirements, but that adds time and separate upgrade semantics.
[00:05:52] Samira Khan: For PHI we probably need the managed private control plane with our own KMS and network controls.
[00:05:57] Alex Chen: Ok noted. We'll map that in the follow-up. Another topic: audit logs and retention — Samira, you wanted specific fields in the logs?
[00:06:05] Samira Khan: We need request/response metadata (request id, model id, timestamp), user identity, and masked PII indicators. Also chain-of-custody info for any exported transcripts.
[00:06:16] Priya Kapoor: We can include those fields. Quick note on masking: model outputs can be post-processed with PII masking; we can support an optional pipeline that redacts likely PHI before storage, but that has accuracy trade-offs.
[00:06:30] Marcus Lee: Would Redwood run the mask in-hosted mode or would masking be customer-side?
[00:06:35] Priya Kapoor: Both options exist. For the strongest guarantee, do masking in your VPC or on-prem before anything leaves your environment. For hosted small-scale, our masking pipeline is available but we recommend validation.
[00:06:47] [00:06:47] Dina Ortiz: About breach notification again — we need clarity on what qualifies as a 'security incident' that triggers the 72-hour window. Also we'll expect a forensics report within 30 days for high-severity incidents.
[00:06:58] Alex Chen: We'll add a definition for 'security incident' in the redline and commit to the 30-day forensic deliverable for high-severity events.
[00:07:05] Marcus Lee: On pricing, is there a procurement playbook you can share? Unit pricing for tokens, embedding, reserved capacity?
[00:07:12] Alex Chen: Yes, we'll share an initial pricing spreadsheet with hosted vs dedicated vs private cost estimates, plus the incremental cost for compliance add-ons like KMS, extended logs, and cross-region replication.
[00:07:22] Priya Kapoor: For benchmarking, if Aurelia wants a POC on PHI-like payloads, we can run a small pilot in Dedicated with synthetic data to measure latency and throughput. That will help decide between dedicated pool sizes.
[00:07:36] Samira Khan: We like that. Timeline: ideally pilot in November. Procurement and legal want contract language first though.
[00:07:45] Alex Chen: Totally. Action plan: Redwood sends a DPA redline this week with explicit 72-hour notif, log retention options, and subprocessor list. We'll also include a baseline pricing sheet and propose dates for a technical deep-dive.
[00:07:59] [00:07:59] Marcus Lee: Can we also get sample SLA language for 99.95 and 99.9 so procurement can evaluate?
[00:08:05] Alex Chen: Yes, we'll include sample SLA clauses and runbook excerpts for failover.
[00:08:11] Dina Ortiz: One more question: data deletion upon contract termination — we need explicit deletion and certification of deletion for PHI.
[00:08:20] Priya Kapoor: We support certified data deletion and provide logs of deletion operations. For hosted, we can offer a deletion certificate and a follow-up attestation. For private, you control retention inside your environment.
[00:08:33] Marcus Lee: Good. I'm going to flag internal stakeholders: legal will review the redline, security will review KMS details, procurement will review SLA prices.
[00:08:43] Alex Chen: Great — do you have a preferred place to exchange the DPA redline? We can use your secure SFT portal, or we can share a link to Redwood's secure doc portal.
[00:08:51] Dina Ortiz: Secure SFTP is preferred for initial legal docs.
[00:08:55] Alex Chen: We'll use SFTP and also post sanitized copies to the secure portal.
[00:08:59] [00:08:59] Priya Kapoor: Quick technical note — for Dedicated, some customers choose quantized models to reduce cost; that can change latency profiles. We'll include a note on model quantization tradeoffs in the tech deep-dive.
[00:09:12] Samira Khan: We're also evaluating whether we can keep inference inside our private data path end-to-end. If Redwood can support on-prem inference without external control plane, that's ideal.
[00:09:22] Priya Kapoor: That's the fully on-prem option I mentioned; it supports isolated inference but requires us to ship a different upgrade and support cadence.
[00:09:30] Marcus Lee: For now let's plan for managed private control plane with our keys.
[00:09:35] Alex Chen: Noted. Ok, before we wrap, I'll summarize the concrete next steps so we're aligned.
[00:09:42] Marcus Lee: go for it.
[00:09:44] Alex Chen: 1) Redwood to send DPA redline with an explicit 72-hour breach notif and proposed indemnity cap language — due 2025-11-03. 2) Redwood to include SOC2 and pen test artifacts via SFTP. 3) Redwood to share pricing spreadsheet including deltas for 99.9 vs 99.95 SLA and cross-region failover. 4) Aurelia to share data classification matrix and designate a compliance owner — due 2025-11-06. 5) Schedule technical deep-dive for week of 2025-11-10 to discuss private deployment and pilot. Anything to add?
[00:10:14] Dina Ortiz: Add: include sample deletion certification language in the redline.
[00:10:18] Alex Chen: Will do.
[00:10:20] Priya Kapoor: I'll prep an architecture sketch for the private managed control plane option.
[00:10:25] Marcus Lee: Good.
[00:10:27] Alex Chen: Thanks everyone. We'll follow up with the artifacts and set a tentative deep-dive calendar invite.
[00:10:33] Samira Khan: Thanks.
[00:10:35] Dina Ortiz: Thanks all.

Call end.
